title: A tap pass arrives at 12.5 m/s instead of 8: the pass beats the skater
pillar: P2 the pass is the fastest thing on the ice
hypothesis: A 15 m tap pass flies 63 frames, and a defender from rest covers 10 m in 64: the pass is no faster than the man who chases it, so thirdjam's hand completes 38 % and the planning hand, which reads the lane, 58 %. thirdjam solves the tap to arrive at 8 m/s (game.pass.power.arrive_mps); at 12.5 the same tap arrives at 13.1 m/s, still under the 14 m/s a body can receive (UJamSim::BodyReceptionMaxSpeed, JamSim.h), and the owner's full-hold pass (a third of the rink, R-0067) is untouched. Expected: passes completed up for both kinds of hand (toward T3's 65 %); taking the pass away costs the planning hand more than before; one-timers up a little (a pass that arrives can be one-timed); the opponents' passes are faster too, so goals against may rise a little; carries, knockdowns and walk-ins do not move.
tempo: the pass's flight against a defender's closing: a 15 m tap 45 f instead of 63 (30 m: 84 instead of 112; 5 m: 9, unchanged) against 10 m from rest in 64 f: the ratio goes from 1.0 to 0.70. Gym: rinklab-thirdlife gym, probe pass.

table: | cell | win % | goal diff | gf/min | ga/min | walk-in goals / match | shots/min | pass compl % | passes/min | one-timers / match | carry s | carries lost % | takes key / no key per min | knockdowns | down s | changes/min | match s | paired: wins pp, goal diff |

why: Half of T3 moved and the game broke around it. Passes that reach a team-mate rose as predicted (thirdjam's regular hand at pro 36.8 -> 56.2 %, its novice 37.9 -> 58.3 %; the planning hand 56.7 -> 64.6 %), and one-timers a little (0.05 -> 0.17 a match for the planning hand). But game.pass.power.arrive_mps is every skater's pass, and the opposing five gained more from it than the human's side: goals for fell and goals against rose at every level, and the ladder collapsed at all-star (thirdjam's regular hand 38.3 -> 6.7 %, paired -31.7 +-7.3; the planning hand 66.7 -> 26.7 %, -40.0 +-8.6); at pro the planning novice lost 26.7 points (+-9.8) and the idle hand at rookie 18.3 (+-8.4). And the pass still does not pay the hand that makes it: without the pass the planning hand won 83.3 % against 71.7 % with it (before the change 81.7 against 85), thirdjam's hand 66.7 against 51.7. A target it did not aim at broke (T8), so it is not kept.
notes: What it taught: (1) completion is a matter of the pass's speed, as the tempo map said; (2) a pass number shared with the bots is a difficulty number in disguise; (3) completing a pass is not the same as the pass paying: the human hands the puck to a mate who plays worse than he does and gives it back in 0.4 of the chances (DifficultyProfile.cpp:19). Follow-ups for round 2, one at a time: the human's own tap alone (a patch), the level's read of a pass (a difficulty number), what the mates do with a pass they get. 60 seeds a cell.
